name: South Route

waypoints.name: Pete Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Self-issue wilderness permit required at the kiosk; Northwest Forest Pass or $5 day-use fee for parking (Cooper Lake Rd / FR-46).
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), turn north on Bullfrog Road for 2.8 miles through two traffic circles, then take SR 903 north through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to the junction with Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 16.8 miles from I-90. Turn left on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about a mile to the Pete Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit are required.

waypoints.name: PCT junction near Lemah Meadow
waypoints.note: Climbers' bypass leaves the Pete Lake Trail/PCT corridor here near 4,000 ft, cutting the Lemah Meadow dogleg to save ~3 miles.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Pete Lake Trail #1323 up the Cooper River on gentle, mostly flat forest tread about 4.5 miles to Pete Lake, then continue to a fork about five miles in and turn right. After about 0.6 mile, turn right again onto the Pacific Crest Trail.

waypoints.name: Vista Lakes (upper lake)
waypoints.note: Established high camp at the upper Vista Lake tarn; warm swimming water and the standard bivy for a summit push.
waypoints.directions: Climb the PCT north up its long series of switchbacks for about 4.5 miles to about 5,500 ft. The Vista Lakes tarns lie just east of the trail at that height; this is the last reliable water.

waypoints.name: Point 5965 / Summit Chief Pass
waypoints.note: Climb easy terrain west of Vista Lakes over Pt. 5965, then drop to Summit Chief Pass and pick up the ridge running northwest toward the peak.
waypoints.directions: Leave the PCT and head cross-country west and north-west from the lakes over easy terrain on Vista Ridge, over Point 5965, then drop to Summit Chief Pass.

waypoints.name: Summit Chief Lake talus basin
waypoints.note: Lower talus basin by a snowfield below Summit Chief Lake; common spot to stash packs before the final climb.
waypoints.directions: From the pass follow the ridge north-west, staying below the cliffs and gendarmes and west of Summit Chief Lake, across sloping slabs cut by slots and gullies into the talus basin south-east of the summit. Dropping to about 6,000 ft to take the scree avoids the worst of the slabs.

waypoints.name: Moat / icy entry gully
waypoints.note: A moat here can be trip-ending after mid-July or in low-snow years; the adjoining gully is often icy in the morning, so carry crampons.
waypoints.directions: Climb steep hardpan, talus and the snowfield below the south-east face toward the point where the mountain steepens at about 7,000 ft and a moat forms. Avoid the first, left-most snow finger, which dead-ends in a deep notch; head for the upper right corner of the snowfield.

waypoints.name: Notch in the south ridge skyline
waypoints.note: Small notch gained by a rising talus traverse; this is the turnaround/gear-swap point for the final loose gully to the top.
waypoints.directions: Past the moat, exit onto steep dirt and scree and take a left-slanting ramp up to the small notch in the south ridge skyline.

waypoints.name: Summit Chief Mountain (true summit)
waypoints.note: True summit on the King/Kittitas county line, 9 miles NE of Snoqualmie Pass; descend by reversing the loose upper gully and steep dirt to the ridge notch.
waypoints.directions: Cross the notch into the southwest gully system: a steep gully, often icy in the morning, then loose rock, steep dirt and a slightly outward-dipping slab. Exit by the gully on the right just below the summit.

approach: Start at the Pete Lake Trailhead (~2,840 ft) at the end of Cooper Lake Road (Forest Road 46) off the Salmon La Sac Road. Follow the Pete Lake Trail (#1323) roughly 4.5 miles of gentle, mostly flat forest walking along the Cooper River to Pete Lake. From Pete Lake, continue up the Lemah Creek/Lemah Meadows drainage (watch for windfall and thick vine maple in the meadow bypass) to join the Pacific Crest Trail; turn right (north) and climb the PCT's long switchback section roughly 4-4.5 more miles to Lower and Upper Vista Lake (~5,500-5,600 ft) — camp is commonly made here, making this a two-day approach of about 9 miles and 2,800 ft to reach the alpine basin. This is also the last reliable water before the high basin — carry extra, as the route above is reported bone-dry until you're back near Vista Lakes. From Vista Lakes, leave the PCT and traverse cross-country north along Vista Ridge toward Summit Chief Pass, crossing a convoluted series of sandstone/siltstone slabs cut by numerous slots and gullies; stay left (west) of Summit Chief Lake and minimize elevation loss while rounding into the southeast basin below the peak. Many parties stash overnight gear around 6,300 ft in the lower talus basin before the final push. From there, traverse steep hardpan and talus (rockfall potential from parties above) up to a notch near 7,200 ft, then work into the southwest gully system — loose rock and an exposed, slightly outward-dipping slab lead through the final Class 2-3 scrambling to the summit. Route-finding through the upper basin and the southwest gully is the crux of the approach; online photos of the south-ridge crossing point are frequently reported as inaccurate, so err toward careful navigation rather than trusting a single beta photo. The route's real crux is often a moat around 7,000 ft where the peak steepens; it can become impassable after mid-July, sometimes earlier in a low-snow year.

pitch_detail.notes: Pete Lake Trailhead to Pete Lake, 4.5 miles.
Pete Lake to Vista Lakes via a Lemah Meadow bypass and the Pacific Crest Trail, roughly 8.5 miles.
Camp to Summit Chief Pass: off-trail traverse north across Vista Ridge into the peak's southeast basin.
Ascend the snowfield/snow finger below the southeast face to gain a notch on the south ridge; the left-most finger dead-ends, requiring a rightward traverse to the upper snowfield corner.
South ridge notch to summit via loose southwest gully/face: steep dirt and scree, a left-slanting ramp, and exposed slab moves on unstable rock to the summit.

itinerary.cal: Vista Lakes basin and the summit basin can hold snow well into July, so most parties climb this July-September; the Pete Lake/Cooper Lake road and trailhead are standard Forest Service access; the only permit is the free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead.

days.note: From the Pete Lake Trailhead on Cooper Lake, hike the flat Pete Lake Trail to Pete Lake (4.5 mi), then join the PCT and climb a long series of switchbacks up to the Vista Lakes tarns just off the trail. It's a long but non-technical day with a full overnight pack.
days.title: Approach to Vista Lakes camp

schedule.label: Leave Pete Lake Trailhead
schedule.detail: Cooper Lake / Salmon La Sac Rd (FR 46) access, ~2,790 ft.

schedule.label: Reach Pete Lake
schedule.detail: Flat trail along the Cooper River.

schedule.label: Join and climb PCT switchbacks
schedule.detail: ~8.5 mi up the Pacific Crest Trail to ~5,500 ft.

schedule.label: Arrive Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Upper lake has sandy/slab sites and swimmable water; ~7.5-8 hr trailhead-to-camp is typical.

days.note: Drop from camp to 5,700 ft Summit Chief Pass, traverse above Summit Chief Lake staying below the ridge/cliffs on the west side, then climb through a high snow basin and up the Southeast Face to a notch on the south ridge. The final ~100 ft is loose Class 2-3 scrambling on untrustworthy rock. Parties describe this as harder than it looks and slower than expected — budget a full day.
days.title: Summit push via Summit Chief Pass and Southeast Face

schedule.label: Leave Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; alpine start for a long, complex day.

schedule.label: Summit Chief Pass (5,700 ft)
schedule.detail: Traverse west below the ridge above Summit Chief Lake.

schedule.label: Enter upper basin below the Southeast Face
schedule.detail: Snow fingers and scree lead toward the south ridge notch.

schedule.label: Summit (7,466 ft)
schedule.detail: Roughly 5.5-6 hr camp-to-summit is typical for competent parties; register shows only a handful of ascents per year.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line — loose rock makes downclimbing the crux slow and careful.

schedule.label: Back at Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: ~11 hr camp-to-camp round trip is typical.

days.objective: Climb to the summit (7,466 ft) and return to Vista Lakes camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: down the PCT switchbacks, past Pete Lake, and out along the Cooper River to the trailhead. Straightforward but long with a lighter pack.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A classic 3-day/2-night backpack: roughly 26-30 miles and ~5,000 ft round trip, with one long, technical summit day from Vista Lakes camp (~11 hr camp-to-camp).

descent_text: This is a walk-off/downclimb — no rappelling is involved on the standard South Route. Reverse the ascent line exactly: downclimb the loose, exposed southwest gully and its outward-dipping slab back to the ~7,200 ft notch, taking care with the loose rock and steep dirt in the upper 500 feet (this section has real rockfall potential for parties below). Continue down through the talus and hardpan to the 6,300 ft basin (recover any stashed gear here), then retrace the slab traverses back onto Vista Ridge and down to Vista Lakes/the PCT. From Vista Lakes, follow the PCT switchbacks back down to Lemah Meadows and the Pete Lake Trail, then out to the Pete Lake Trailhead. Some parties vary the return by continuing along the PCT to Waptus Lake and crossing Waptus Pass back to the Pete Lake trailhead as an alternate loop. Total car-to-car mileage for the round trip runs approximately 30-33+ miles depending on exact line, so most parties treat this as an overnight with a basin or Vista Lakes camp rather than a single push.
